admission_apply.text: Breath finds the bore. A dry tick answers from farther off than this reed can reach.

native.admission_inspect: A thumb-length reed, salt-stiff, bore gone oval. The shadow lies a finger longer than the wood.
apply_texts: A second pale track stops short of the bore. The tick follows it and arrives thin and late.
Again the reed is only a reed. The late tick still comes, but the hand is steadier for the limit.
Breath finds the bore. A dry tick answers from farther off than this reed can reach.
One clear patch takes the breath. The tick is close, then thins out farther than the reed.
Salt powders under the thumb. The tick comes late, and nearer than the long shadow.
Sounding it, you hear the interval before the tick. The interval is longer than the reed.
The crust cracks at a new place. The tick is the same, only it seems to have traveled.
The reed is plainly small. That smallness settles the fingers more than the long shadow does.
The reed takes breath and returns the same dry tick. The salt does not shift again.
The same tick, a little thinner. A new pale track in the salt stops, then seems to resume smaller.
inspect_texts: A hairline has opened in the salt. Along it the wood looks older than the rest of the reed.
A second pale scrape crosses the salt and stops. The shadow still overruns the cut end.
A thumb-length reed, salt-stiff, bore gone oval. The shadow lies a finger longer than the wood.
Even salt ridges tally something the hand cannot finish. The bore looks deeper than the cut.
Salt crusts a small reed. The grain is palm-worn, as if carried farther than its length allows.
Salt has nearly sealed a thumb-length reed. What remains of the bore throws a long, thin shadow.
Short in the palm, the reed seems to continue past its cut. Salt has sealed one split like a scar.
The crust is thumbed thin in two places. Neither pale track quite reaches the oval bore.
The salt ridges are too even for weather. They tally a distance this small reed does not hold.
Thumbed tracks cross the crust and stop at the bore. One of them seems to begin again, smaller.
native.name: Salt-stiff Reed
